history.summary: A 2BR at Kovan Grandeur priced at $1,147 PSF, a striking ~16% below the $1,372 URA median — but the URA 5yr rate is negative (-0.6%/yr over 34 txns), so the discount may reflect a genuinely weak price trend rather than a bargain. Sub-$1.1M ticket near Kovan MRT keeps it liquid, but appreciation is the worry.
history.rating_rationale: Negative -0.59%/yr appreciation across a credible 34-txn sample is the core problem — this development has not appreciated. The 16% gap below median PSF could be a motivated seller or could be the unit/stack being inferior; worth scrutiny. 810m to Kovan NEL MRT is walkable-ish but not prime. Affordable D19 entry with a deep HDB-upgrader pool supports liquidity, but no catalyst to reverse the flat trend.

history.summary: The algo's headline 'deep bargain' (-30.5% age-adj, -22% cohort, very_low_psf) is a DATA QUIRK built on a 2-transaction cohort. Verified comps show the ask is actually a slight PREMIUM, not a discount — and the project carries real quality and liquidity problems.
history.rating_rationale: This is exactly the thin-cohort trap v3.4 warns about: psf_cohort_txns=2 and a -22% cohort premium are not trustworthy. The decisive verification: a 915 sqft unit at Kovan Grandeur transacted on 5 Dec 2025 at S$1,038 psf / S$950,000 — so the S$1,147 psf / S$1,050,000 ask is roughly a 10% PREMIUM to the most recent same-size comp, the opposite of the algo's claim. The project's overall recent average (~S$1,522 psf) is inflated by tiny 388/431/570 sqft units; pooling those into the 915 sqft cohort manufactured the phantom discount. On top of the false value signal: resident reviews cite poor management, unrepaired defects and paint peeling onto cars; it is a small 74-unit development (thin resale liquidity and weak en-bloc/AGM governance); and it is 99-yr leasehold from 2010, not freehold. The appreciation_pct of -0.59% on 34 txns also flags weak momentum. No catalyst justifies overriding all of this.
red_flags: DATA QUIRK: -22% cohort discount rests on only 2 transactions; not a real bargain
Ask S$1,147 psf is ~10% ABOVE the verified 5 Dec 2025 same-size (915 sqft) transaction at S$1,038 psf
Resident reviews: poor management, broken/unfixed facilities, paint peeling onto parked cars
Tiny 74-unit development — thin resale liquidity and weak governance
99-year leasehold from 2010 (algo/listing context implied freehold — it is NOT freehold)
Negative trailing appreciation (-0.59%) — weak local momentum
catalysts: Near Kovan MRT and Heartland Mall (the only genuine plus)

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Project-level yield is quoted ~4.6%, but that is buoyed by very small high-PSF units; a 915 sqft 2BR bought at a premium to comps would deliver a weaker effective yield. Poor maintenance also pressures achievable rent.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Trailing -0.59% CAGR signals flat-to-negative momentum, and there is no relative-value edge (the unit is priced above comps). With small-development illiquidity and maintenance issues, forward appreciation is below-average — Avoid.
